Commissioner Apodaca called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the
Norwalk City Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the
provisions of Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call in person were Commissioner
Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia and Commissioner Navas and, via Zoom, Vice Chair
Lopez. Chair Barragan was absent. Also present were John P. Ramirez, Director of
Community Development; Nvair Deukmejian, Deputy City Attorney; Jill Ann Arabe,
Development Services Manager; Ilianna Padilla, Planning Technician; Andrew Arellano,
Assistant Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of October 25,
2023 with Commissioner Navas abstaining as he was absent at that meeting.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2023-02
CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 2023-05
David A. Storer, Quick Quack (“Applicant”); a request to permit the construction of a new
one-story 3,511 square foot carwash facility and associated site improvements on a 1.0
acre site. The subject property is generally known as 11642 Firestone Boulevard,
located at the terminus of Woods Avenue and the west side of Firestone Boulevard
(also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8048-007-002), in the General
Commercial (C-3) zone. The project includes a request for:
(1) Precise Development Plan No. 2023-02: To permit the construction of a new building
  and associated site improvements; and
(2) Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-05: To permit an express carwash facility; and
(3) Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15303 (New Construction or
  Conversion of Small Structures).

Commissioner Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Planning Technician Padilla
presented a report stating that the request is to permit a new, one-story, 3,511 square
foot commercial building and associated site improvements to operate a carwash facility
known as Quick Quack Car Wash; that the one-acre project site has a General Plan
designation of General Commercial and zoning of General Commercial (C-3); that the
subject site has been vacant since 2019; that the proposed commercial building is located
at the center of the property; that it is designed to comply with the minimum setbacks,
building height and architectural design standards; that new parking spaces are provided
north of the building, closer to the street, for convenient customer and employee access
and to buffer sensitive uses from potential noise impacts; that parking stalls with vacuums
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

are provided south of the building for customer usage only; that other site improvements
include upgraded landscaping, bike racks, canopies over the pay station and vacuums,
as well as a trash enclosure located southeast of the building; that signage for the site is
also proposed which includes channel letter wall signs and a monument sign to the north
entrance of the site; that the floor plan includes the car wash tunnel, equipment room,
employee lounge, office and a restroom; that in consideration of the community’s
comments received at the community meeting and of the vision and goals of the City,
staff recommends denial of the project as it is not consistent with the General Plan nor
serve the public convenience and welfare; that the subject site is identified as a housing
opportunity site in the draft Housing Element and the proposed use will not be compatible
with existing uses and development anticipated for the area within the Heart of Norwalk
Specific Plan; that multiple car washes already exist within close proximity of the subject
site and adding the proposed car wash will not increase the positive image of Norwalk;
that City efforts to provide a wide array of local amenities along the Firestone Corridor
and opportunities for housing will be discouraged as a result of the project.

Further, Miss Padilla indicated that the applicant submitted a letter addressed to the
Planning Commission outlining the reasons why the project should not be denied, and
that the letter was forwarded to the Commission this morning. Further, she stated that
based on the aforementioned concerns, staff recommends that the Planning Commission
adopt Resolution Nos. 23-33 and 23-34 to deny the applicant’s request.

David A. Storer stated that he is the representative of Quick Quack, and that he is here
to discuss the merits of the project and, ultimately, to request that the Commission direct
staff to return with resolutions approving the project. He indicated that the main bullet
points are with respect to the administrative record and the General Plan; that the General
Plan comes in two main pieces, the General Plan map and the policies that direct the
development of the City of Norwalk with respect to goals, policies, objectives and
implementation measures; that in his letter he identifies pages and objectives where the
project is consistent; that the Firestone area is intended to have automobile uses and
related uses; that the General Plan policy talks about the revitalization and enhancement
of existing uses; that his point tonight is that the project is consistent with the General
Plan; and that there is no evidence in the record to demonstrate that it is incompatible
with the General Plan other than a declarative statement saying so.

Mr. Storer further stated that he would like to point out that the Vision of the City of Norwalk
is identified in the General Plan as a policy document; that the staff report talks about
consistency with the Zoning Code whether it is with respect to traffic, and noise, and that
the project would be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) were
it to be approved; that the merits of the project is not based on popularity but on the
governing documents of the City of Norwalk; that he recognizes that a Conditional Use
Permit is a discretionary land use entitlement, but that the project is in the C-3 Zone which
looks into the compatibility with the neighborhood; that the commercial zone is compatible
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

with the neighborhood as there are car washes nearby further down the street; that they
have done market research indicating that a Quick Quack car wash at this location would
be frequented by the residents; that, as he stated in his letter, the project has met the
findings of the General Plan and consistency with the Zoning Code; that he also pointed
out that it is consistent with the Heart of Norwalk Vision Plan; that this project must not be
reviewed with respect to a Specific Plan that has not yet been adopted; that the staff
report presentation makes reference to the property being vacant; that it has not been
vacant since 2019, and that the land owner’s representative, Ross Melodia, is here to
address that; that he also pointed out in his letter that there is no interest from the land
owner to develop residential; and that the site is not readily available or vacant as
represented in the City’s Housing Element; and that, again, he would request that the
Commission direct staff to return with two resolutions approving the project.

Ross Melodia stated that he is here on behalf of the owner of the property in support of
the applicant and the car wash use; that, prior to the meeting, he submitted a letter with
attachments from the landlord in regards to this matter; that it was emailed this morning
but, somehow, the email did not go through; that the property at 11642 Firestone
Boulevard has been owned by Casa de Normandie South, LLC since 2013; that they are
a small family-owned company; that, historically, this site had issues in finding quality
tenants due to the challenges of the surrounding area, such as homelessness; that some
examples of that are provided in the packet that he submitted to the Commission; that,
contrary to the staff report, the building has been occupied consistently; that the current
tenant, American Family Housing, has been there since 2019; that the packet includes a
picture of the building, which he took yesterday, with their name on the front and cars
everywhere.

Continuing with his presentation, Mr. Melodia indicated that the property is zoned C-3
which conditionally permits a car wash; that the site is surrounded by pretty intense uses;
that there is a recycling center to the east; that, to the west, there is a pretty run-down
98cents store; that located behind to the south is a truck storage facility; that directly
across the street there is an apartment complex; that to the west of that, there is another
car wash; that to the east of the apartment complex there is an auto mechanics repair
shop, a tattoo shop, an auto body shop, dry cleaners and a plumbing shop; that the Quick
Quack Car Wash would be an upgrade to the area; that they were surprised by staff’s
recommendation to deny the use; that they believe that staff’s recommendation does not
comply with the City’s current codes for the location for the Specific Plan or the Heart of
Norwalk Vision Plan; that, as mentioned by David Storer, it does allow these
developments to include both commercial and/or residential development and not
residential only; that staff indicated that they oppose the use because of the community
opposition; that the August 29, 2023 community meeting was mentioned; that he attended
that meeting at which nine (9) residents provided testimony; that none of the individuals
were from the immediate vicinity of the project; that they believe staff made that
recommendation as it is their hope that someday this property, along with the adjacent
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 4
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

ones, will be redeveloped into a strictly residential use; that the City Council has not yet
adopted a Specific Plan or changed the zoning to reflect that use; that it is their belief that
the market should determine the type of tenants for this property; that they are urging the
Commission to take this under consideration; that, from an owner’s standpoint, the
economic damage that the owner may possibly incur as a result of staff’s decision could
be severe and irreversible; that they looked at the City’s own projection of the residential
land values and found that with the de facto rezoning of the use it will reduce the current
value of the owner’s property immediately by 35 percent; that the property owner has a
real stake and can be hurt severely by this decision; that, in summary, the project will only
create a positive addition to the area, and that they would ask that the Commission direct
staff to return with resolutions to support the project at the next meeting. Further, he
thanked the Commission for their time and consideration, and he asked the Commission
to look through the packet that they provided so that they fully understand the impact that
the denial will have.

In response to Commissioner Apodaca’s comment for clarification on the 35 percent
reduction, Mr. Melodia shared that in 2021, the City projected the land values for
residential in the redevelopment area around $69.00 per square foot which, since then
various factors have come into play increasing the cost of redeveloping a property
especially into residential; that they believe that the $69.00 per square foot number is not
a good number anymore; that it is lower based on all the market conditions; that with the
Quick Quack Car Wash going in there, and the value of the property that will be created
by that business being there, they are looking at a value for that property of approximately
$106.00 per square foot; that even if they used the $69.00 per square foot projection that
the City showed in 2021, they are looking at about a 35% reduction in the value; that they
believe that this is a significant number, especially as a property owner; and he stated
that there are more details in the packet that they provided.

Mr. Storer commented on the number of emails received in opposition to the project which
contained information relative to the number of car washes and the concentration of
existing facilities which, again, is not a criteria of the General Plan as there is no policy
adopted by the City Council or Planning Commission to even indicate what is a positive
image of the City of Norwalk.

Norwalk resident Lisa stated that the City does not need another car wash as there are
enough car washes in Norwalk.

Norwalk resident Jessie shared that she is against the car wash; and she shared that the
added traffic would negatively impact the area residents. Further, she indicated that she
attended the community meeting in August; and that Dora Sandoval also submitted an
email in opposition tonight (which was received after the start of the meeting).
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 5
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

Responding to the two comments just made in opposition, Mr. Storer stated that they are
valuable; however, the concept of “we don’t need it” is really a market decision and not a
popularity contest; that they know that the community will support this car wash at the
subject location; that they did market studies and provided a traffic study, which is
available to the members of the public; that they have shown that they are consistent with
the traffic analysis and with the sound studies.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Commissioner Apodaca
closed the public hearing.

Commissioner Garcia stated that this is not about the number of car washes, although he
agrees that there are too many car washes in Norwalk; that it is more about the vision;
that they cannot change the past, but that they can continue to proceed with a new vision
and responsible development as they move forward; that he does not believe that this
development is good for Norwalk; that there is an existing car wash across the street
which he would not have approved; that he understands where the applicant is coming
from; however, what they need is responsible development to be consistent with the
vision where Norwalk is going; and that he supports staff’s recommendation.

Commissioner Navas shared that the car wash would be an improvement as to what is
going on at the site as there is a severe issue with homelessness; that he, too,
understands what the tenant is going through; that there was never a vision for that
corridor of Norwalk; that he agrees with Commissioner Garcia’s comment that the other
car wash is located at a poor site; that the City is trying to bring in quality housing and to
have more cohesion when it comes to the development of the City and that particular
corridor; that he knows for a fact in talking with the people in the community that they do
not want car washes, liquor stores, and check cashing places; that they want the City to
change; that, again, the applicant is in a tough situation; however, they need to fall in line
with what the community wants; and that he thanked the two residents for attending the
meeting.

Vice Chair Lopez stated that she, too, agrees that there are too many car washes in this
City; that, as Commissioner Navas indicated, the residents that she talked to want to see
a change in this community; and that she supports staff’s recommendation.

Commissioner Apodaca stated that a vision is very important; that one vision being
brought up is the Heart of Norwalk; that the City is looking for quality businesses that the
residents need, including housing; that when they talked about attendance at the last
community meeting, a comment was made about stakeholders and who showed up at
that meeting; that everyone is a stakeholder when the City is only nine square miles; that
every resident is affected by any development in this City; that regarding the applicant’s
comment on marketing, she strongly feels that a lot of the City’s thoroughfares, such as
Firestone, Imperial and Rosecrans are much like highways that run parallel to the 91 and
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 6
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

5 freeways; that a lot of these motorists do not live in this City and, in her opinion, those
people would be the ones frequenting the car washes.

It was moved by Commissioner Garcia and seconded by Commissioner Navas to: (1)
adopt Resolution No. 23-33 to deny Precise Development Plan No. 2023-02; and (2)
adopt Resolution No. 23-34 to deny Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-05.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE:
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas
  and Vice Chair Lopez
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Chair Barragan

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2023-03
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2023-11
Markie Anderle, Raising Cane’s (“Applicant”); a request to permit a new 3,705 square
foot drive-through restaurant on a 1.60 acre site. The subject property is generally
known as 12666 Studebaker Road, located on the southeast corner of Imperial Highway
and Studebaker Road (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8050-032-
032), in the Restricted Commercial (C-1) zone). The project includes a request for:
(1) Precise Development Plan No. 2023-03: To permit the construction of a new
  commercial building; and
(2) Director Approval Request No. 2023-11: To permit a drive-through establishment;
  and
(3) Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15303
  (New Construction of Small Structures).

Commissioner Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Assistant Planner Arellano
presented a report stating that the request is to permit the construction of a new 3,705
square foot Raising Cane’s restaurant with a drive-through component; that the site
consists of 1.60 acres with a General Plan designation of Neighborhood Commercial
and zoning of Restricted Commercial (C-1); that the project is located at the southeast
corner of Imperial Highway and Studebaker Road; that the site currently contains a
vacant building previously occupied by a CVS Pharmacy; that the building will be
located closer to the street intersection, which offers improved pedestrian access,
outdoor dining opportunities, and adequate screening of the drive-through lanes; that
the site will be served by two driveways, one each on Studebaker Road and Imperial
Highway; that the drive-through lanes can support a queuing of ten cars in one lane
from the entrance to the pickup window; and that it is not anticipated that the drive-
through lanes would impact through traffic on Studebaker Road or Imperial Highway.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 7
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

Further, Assistant Planner Arellano shared that the applicant requested that Condition
No. 5 of Resolution No. 23-32, which makes reference to exterior speakers, be modified
by adding language “except that speakers may be permitted on the exterior dining patio
only playing low-level ambient, non-amplified music”; that, in summary, the proposed
project will enhance the surrounding area by revitalizing a vacant site and providing a
local-serving commercial use compatible with the neighborhood; that the project
complies with applicable development standards of the Norwalk Municipal Code and is
consistent with the General Plan vision; and that staff recommends that the Commission
adopt Resolution Nos. 23-31 and 23-32 approving the project subject to the revised
conditions.

Sara Holmes, HD Group, stated that she would like to provide some background
information; that Raising Cane’s was founded by Todd Graves in 1996; that his first
restaurant was located on the LSU campus in Baton Rouge, Louisiana; that he brought
his dog to work and that is how he came up with the name; that Raising Cane’s has a
unique concept as their focus is on “One Love” which applies to the quality of the food
as well as the passion shown by staff who renew their training every year; that they also
make sure that the employees have competitive wages and that, recently, they have
implemented a first-time home buying policy giving employees a chance at having
$10,000 put down on a new home; that besides bringing new jobs to the community
they are trying to give back to schools and to charities, with a focus on pet welfare.

Further, she commented on the restaurant’s security features indicating that, when
vehicles are pulling into the site, the crew can see them from their windows; that the
average turn-around time for orders are two minutes and twenty-eight seconds which is
the fastest time in the industry; that they want to design a site that is not just aesthetically
pleasing but also has a lot of functionality; that they have two drive-through lanes; that
they make sure that they have on-site traffic management for queuing cars; that on the
second drive-through lane, during peak hours, they would have a crew actively assist;
and that should queuing occur past the order point, crew members would be taking
orders.

Markie Anderle, Three6ixty, stated that she is working on the design; that, as Sara
Holmes mentioned, Caine’s takes it commitment to the community very seriously, which
included collaboration with the Planning Department; that some of the changes that
were incorporated based on feedback from staff were additional low-lighting areas;
relocation of tables from the west side of the property to the north; an agreement to
review security operations after six months to evaluate if additional measures are
needed; right-in and right-out of the Studebaker driveway in preparation of the grand
opening plan to ensure smooth operations from day one; that the project has been
thoughtfully designed to beautify the corner of the intersection and ensure appropriate
transition from commercial to residential use by substantial landscape buffers; that the
commercial area along the street frontage will also be enhanced through landscaping;
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 8
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

that the building and patio spaces have been located as far away as possible from
neighboring uses; that, as discussed, the project has been designed with ample
landscaping, outdoor dining, a double drive-through lane, handicap parking spaces and
bicycle parking spaces; that the interior has been designed to create a high-level dining
experience; that the plan includes substantial screening of the patio area from the street
to enhance the pedestrian environment and create a pleasant experience for diners and
passersby; that, as staff has noted, they would like to modify Condition No. 5 to allow
low-level non amplified music in the exterior patio area; that any sound from these
speakers will be buffered by traffic noise, and that the sound will be directed towards
the interior of the site. Ms. Anderle stated that on behalf of the applicant’s team, she
would like to thank staff for all of their hard work and collaboration on this project.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Commissioner
Apodaca closed the public hearing.

In response to Commissioner Garcia’s question if all of the Raising Cane’s restaurants
are open until 3:00 a.m. Ms. Holmes replied that in California they are open until 3:30
a.m. and that the dining area generally closes at 2:00 a.m. Commissioner Garcia
indicated that, for him, a 2:00 a.m. closing time is late enough.

Commissioner Navas asked if they have given any thought to where the parking would
start as an overflow would spill over into Studebaker; and if consideration has been
given to increasing the height of the wall adjacent to residential to help with the noise
level or will it stay the same size.

Another representative, via Zoom, shared that the wall will stay the same; that they are
including more landscaping in the area to reduce the noise and visibility into the homes
to the south.

Ms. Anderle commented on the queuing and parking. She stated that if there is backup,
it actually backs up into their own parking lot before it even hits the public street; that
beyond the 24 cars that the actual drive-through lanes will hold, the site probably holds
another 20 cars for queuing which is way beyond any fast food location; that regarding
the wall, there is a fifteen foot landscape buffer plus the new driveway; that the drive-
through is 40 feet away from the nearest residential property and another almost 10 feet
to any structure; and that this is actually a larger buffer than the one CVS had.

Director Ramirez stated that in response to Commissioner Navas’ comment on
increasing the height of the wall, should the adjacent residents have any issues, staff
can come back to the Commission and find a solution.

Commissioner Navas stated that it is a great project and an improvement to the site;
and that none of the residents responded to the public hearing notice.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 9
Minutes of the Special Meeting  November 8, 2023

Commissioner Apodaca shared that she believes that Raising Cane’s is going to be a
very good neighbor; that the landscaping that has been shown is going to be a great
buffer; that the building’s position is the furthest away from the neighborhood; that the
project is going to be very attractive and much needed; and that she is hoping that this
is the beginning of the revitalization of the four corners; that regarding the hours of
operation, she has no problem with the facility being open until 3:00 a.m. with the
audible adjustment for the drive-through; that should complaints be received regarding
the hours of operation, noise or with the wall, the Commission can always revisit the
project.

Vice Chair Lopez stated that she likes everything about the project as presented as it is
modern and is going to benefit the community; and that she supports staff’s
recommendation for approval.

It was moved by Commissioner Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Navas to: (1)
Adopt Resolution No. 23-31 to approve Precise Development Plan No. 2023-03 subject
to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-
32 to approve Director Approval Request No. 2023-11 subject to the Conditions of
Approval contained in Exhibit “A”, and that language be added to Condition No. 5 to
allow low-level non amplified music in the exterior patio area; that any sound from these
speakers will be buffered by traffic noise, and that the sound will be directed towards
the interior of the site; and (3 Consider and find that the project is exempt from the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section
15303 (New Construction of Small Structures).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE:
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas
  and Vice Chair Lopez
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Chair Barragan

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The project involves two sites located at 12156 Front Street (also known as Assessor’s Parcel
Number (“APN”) 8056-016-007) and 12169 Front Street (also known as Assessor’s Parcel
Number (“APN”) 8056-014-003, -004 & -005), which are both owned by the same property
owner, Mr. Guadelupe Gomez. The sites are 0.18 acres and 0.27 acres respectively, have a
General Plan designation of General Commercial and zoning of Commercial Manufacturing
(C-M). They are located on the north and south sides of Front Street, across the street from
each other, between Clarkdale Ave. and Funston Ave. Surrounding the project sites are a mix
of commercial and light industrial uses and other assembly uses. The property at 12156 Front
Street has been vacant for nearly a decade and was previously a retail establishment for a
seafood business. The property at 12169 Front Street is operating as a church, without prior
city approvals, with a congregation of about 12-15 people.

Public Notification

The applicant and property owner hosted a community meeting on October 5, 2023, at the
Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex. Only one community member attended the meeting and
expressed concerns about the limited parking availability on-site for the banquet hall facility,
but were overall excited about the revitalization of these vacant properties. Their parking
concerns were addressed with the understanding of the proposed shared parking and the
hours of operations of the banquet facility outside of normal business hours. Public hearing
notices were published in the Norwalk Patriot and posted at locations set forth in NMC Section
1.08.030 as well as mailed to 186 property owners and occupants within 500 feet of the
property on December 1, 2023. As of the writing of this report, staff has received no public
comments.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project will not have a
significant effect on the environment and is listed as Section 15303 Categorical Exemption.
Section 15303 consists of construction and location of limited number of new, small facilities
or structures; installation of small new equipment and facilities in small structures; and the
conversion of existing small structures from one use to another where only minor modifications
are made in the exterior of the structure. The proposed project involves the conversion of two
existing buildings into a banquet hall and church in conjunction with parking lot modifications.

SUMMARY

The proposed development will enhance the surrounding area by revitalizing and activating
two existing buildings for assembly uses. The banquet hall will provide opportunities for the
community to rent and utilize for special events such as birthdays, weddings, and meetings.

SUBJECT: Director Approval Request No. 2023-14 to permit the on-site sale and consumption of
  alcohol (beer and wine) within a 2,357 square foot restaurant and 560 square foot
  outdoor dining area. Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from
  CEQA pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities), licensing, operation, or minor
  alterations to an existing facility. The subject site is 12539 Imperial Highway, Suite 101
  located at the northwest corner of Imperial Highway and Bloomfield Avenue.

RECOMMENDATION

That the Planning Commission:

1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-38 to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2023-14
subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and

2. Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) Guidelines pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities), which includes among
other things, licensing, operation, or minor alterations to an existing facility.

AUTHORITY

Section 17.02.203.C of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Director of
Community Development (“Director”) to permit the on-sale alcohol sales within bona fide

restaurants as defined in NMC Section 17.04.140. The Director may refer any request to the
Planning Commission for review and determination.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The subject site is located at the northwest corner of Imperial Highway and Bloomfield Avenue
in the Professional and Office (P/O) zone, and has a General Plan designation of Professional
Office. It is surrounded by offices to the west and south (across Imperial Highway),
Metropolitan State Hospital to the north, and commercial to the east (City of Santa Fe Springs).
The Norwalk Fitness Village shopping center includes a fitness gym, dentist office, and eating
establishments. It was developed in 2018 and the existing space was previously occupied by
a Pick Up Stix restaurant, ending operations in Spring of 2023.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting to permit the on-site sale and consumption of alcohol (Type-41 on-
sale beer and wine) within a 2,357 sq. ft. restaurant (California Fish Grill) and 560 sq. ft. outdoor
dining area. The restaurant will be open daily. As part of the project, the applicant is proposing
the following hours of operation: Monday through Saturday from 10:00 am to 10:00 pm and
Sundays from 10:00 am to 9:00 pm. The sale of alcohol is proposed to begin at 11:00 am and
end 30 minutes before closing time. This practice is consistent with the existing Chipotle
Mexican Grill, which closes at 10:00 pm daily, and the recently approved Mountain Mike’s
Pizza restaurant, which has a closing time of 9:00 pm on Sundays through Thursdays, and a
closing time of 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

Tenant improvement plans, which include an interior remodel of the restaurant and exterior
remodel to the existing patio, are currently in plan check with the Building and Safety Division.
According to the applicant, the new restaurant is tentatively scheduled to open in June 2024.
Once in operation the restaurant will have a total of 25 employees, with five employees per
shift.

California Fish Grill is a fast casual restaurant offering seafood dishes with 47 locations, across
three different states: Arizona, California and Nevada. The restaurant is currently operating
two existing locations nearby in the cities of Downey and Cerritos, and both of these locations
hold Type 41 licenses. The new restaurant includes an existing 560 square feet outdoor dining
area surrounded by 42 inch high wood fencing (similar to Panera Bread). The sale and
consumption of beer and wine will occur inside the building and within the outdoor dining area.
It will operate ancillary to the primary food service and is not anticipated to generate negative
impacts to surrounding uses. The applicant is proposing pre-recorded ambient music to play
in the outdoor patio area.

staff recommends approval with conditions that address the following issues:

  •  Limiting hours of operation
  •  Providing surveillance system and lighting for the site
  •  Training and education for employees regarding alcohol sales

General Plan’s policies related to the Professional/Office Land Use category. The project
encourages economic growth of a local business and development of a shopping center, which
is important for providing adequate local serving commercial uses.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project will not have a
significant effect on the environment per Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA
Guidelines. Section 15301 consists of operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, licensing or
minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features involving negligible or no expansion of existing use. The project involves
on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine within a restaurant.

SUMMARY

The proposed project complies with all applicable regulations and, as conditioned, will not be
detrimental to the public health, safety and welfare of surrounding uses. The request will create
a more vibrant commercial center, occupy a vacant space, and promote the economic viability
of the restaurant. The alcohol service will be limited to hours of operation that will not negatively
impact the community. Staff recommends approval of the project with suggested conditions of
approval.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: To permit the on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine
(Type 41 license) within an existing 2,357 square feet restaurant and a 560 square feet
outdoor dining area.

The following is a list of code requirements deemed applicable to the proposed project based
on plans stated above. The list is intended to assist the applicant by identifying requirements,
which must be satisfied during the various stages of project permitting and implementation.
A list of conditions of approval adopted by the Planning Commission in conjunction with the
requested entitlement(s), if any, will also be provided upon final project approval. If you have
any questions regarding these requirements, please contact the Plan Reviewer.

  1. Development Standards and Operations (NMC 17.04.140.G1)

  a. Alcohol must be served at the counter by employees of the restaurant and sold
  for on-site consumption.

  b. Gross monthly sales of alcohol shall not exceed gross monthly sales of food
  and other non-alcohol items within the same period. The licensee shall at all
  times maintain records, which reflect separately the gross sale of food and the
  gross sales of alcoholic beverages of the licensed business. Said reports shall
  be kept no less frequently than on a quarterly basis and shall be made
  available to the City on demand.

  c. Entertainment in conjunction with the restaurant is limited to indoor ambient
  music to compliment the dining experience, and shall be limited to background
  music at a low volume that is not audible outside of the building. The
  establishment shall remain in compliance with Title 9, Chapter 9.04, Article
  Ill.Noise.
 d. No employee or agent shall be permitted to accept money or any other thing
  of value from a customer for the purpose of sitting or otherwise spending time
  with customers while in the premises, nor shall the licensee/petitioner provide
  or permit, or make available either gratuitous or for compensation, male or
  female persons who act as escorts, companions, or guests of and for the
  customers.

e. Licensee/petitioner shall not require an admission charge or a cover charge,
  nor shall there be a requirement to purchase a minimum number of drinks.

f. The premises shall be maintained as a restaurant and shall provide a menu
  containing an assortment of food as offered in such restaurants.

g. During normal meal hours, the business shall be designed and used for and
  must possess the necessary utensils, table service, and condiment dispensers
  with which to serve meals to the public.

h. Any graffiti painted or marked upon the premises shall be removed or painted
  over to match the color of the surface to which it is applied within forty eight
  (48) hours of the discovery thereof.

i.  Applicant will cooperate with the prosecution of offenders who engage in
  unlawful activity on site.

j.  The owner, manager, or person in charge of the establishment shall be twenty-
  one (21) years or older. At least one such person shall be present on the
  premises at all times. No person under the age of eighteen (18) shall sell or
  serve alcoholic beverages.

k. The restaurant shall be responsible for maintaining the premises and adjoining
  rights-of-way free of debris and litter.

l.  The restaurant shall be responsible for monitoring both patron and employee
  conduct on the premises and within the parking areas under its control to
  prevent behavior that adversely affects or detracts from the quality of life for
  adjoining residents, property owners, and businesses.

m. All trash and recycling bins under control of the restaurant shall be kept closed
  and locked at all times when they are not in use, and shall be maintained such
  that they do not overflow.

n. Loitering is prohibited on all areas under the control of the restaurant. A "No
  Loitering or Public Drinking" sign that is a minimum of four by six inches shall
  be posted outside next to every exit.
 o. A minimum of one on-duty manager with authority over the activities within the
  restaurant shall be on the premises at all times that the restaurant is open for
  business. The on-duty manager's responsibilities shall include the monitoring
  of the premises to ensure compliance with all applicable State laws, Municipal
  Code requirements and the conditions imposed by the Department of
  Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC). The restaurant shall be responsible for
  discouraging illegal and criminal activity on the subject premises and any
  exterior area under its control.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: To permit the on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine
(Type 41 license) within an existing 2,357 square feet restaurant and a 560 square feet
outdoor dining area.

The following is a list of code requirements deemed applicable to the proposed project based
on plans stated above. The list is intended to assist the applicant by identifying requirements,
which must be satisfied during the various stages of project permitting and implementation.
A list of conditions of approval adopted by the Planning Commission in conjunction with the
requested entitlement(s), if any, will also be provided upon final project approval. If you have
any questions regarding these requirements, please contact the Plan Reviewer.

  1. Beer and wine sales may commence at 11:00am and must end 30 minutes before
  closing, all days of the week. Alcohol may be consumed in their designated outdoor
  patio dining area. Alcoholic beverages cannot be served to or consumed by a patron
  who is not seated, or to anyone when the restaurant kitchen is closed.

  2. Gross monthly sales of alcohol shall not exceed gross monthly sales of food and
  other non-alcoholic items with the same period.

  3. All employees involved with the sale of alcohol, are to complete a Responsible
  Beverage Server (RBS) training course approved by the California Department of
  Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) and City of Norwalk, Department of Public Safety
  within six (6) months of Director's Approval Request (DAR) or an employee' start
  date, whichever occurs last. Visit ABC website to find a RBS course provided
  https://www.abc.ca.gov/programs/RBS.html
 4. Business manager and employees involved with the sale of alcohol, must attend the
  ABC Licensee Education on Alcohol and Drugs (LEAD) Program which is a free
  prevention and education program for retail licensees and their employees. Program
  must be completed within six (6) months of approval of the Directors Approval
  Request or an employee's start date, whichever occurs later. The curriculum is
  designed for licensees, managers and employees. Program length is 4 hours.

5. No happy hour, nor drink specials or other bar promotions are permitted to be
  advertised outside or in the window/door areas.

6. No live entertainment shall be provided.

7. A surveillance camera system plan shall be submitted for review and approval by
  the Public Safety and Community Development Directors.

  a. The surveillance camera system is to be maintained operational at all times,
  including during non-business hours. The system features and functions shall
  be accessible by business management staff at all times during normal
  business hours. The system shall provide a video feed of sufficient quality to
  permit the Public Safety Department and Norwalk Sheriff's Station to utilize
  the feed for law enforcement purposes, whether emergency or investigatory.
  Business shall ensure all video recordings/feeds remain accessible on a
  Digital Video Recording system for a minimum of thirty (30) days.
  b. Business shall make all video stored on the Digital Video Recording system
  available to the Public Safety and Norwalk Sheriff's Station at any time. The
  Public Safety and/or Sheriff's Station may request copies of recorded videos.
  Business must provide the requested video recording within twenty-four (24)
  hours of the Public Safety/Sheriff's request.
  c. Surveillance cameras shall be placed in a position to provide visual coverage
  of all entrances/exits, cash registers, safes, office/storage areas, and adjacent
  parking areas.

8. A security plan shall be submitted for review and approval by the Director of Public
  Safety or his/her designee prior to the issuance of permit(s).

9. A lighting plan shall be submitted for review and approval by the Public Safety and
  Community Development Departments. Security lighting shall be provided on all
  sides of the exterior of the building. All inoperable lighting shall be repaired/replaced
  within twenty-four (24) hours to ensure adequate lighting is in place at all times.
  Inoperable parking lot lighting adjacent to the business shall be reported to the
  property manager for repair/replacement.

10.Business shall participate in the Department of Public Safety's Business Watch
  program and anti-trespassing/enforcement program (S.H.A.P.E), which includes
  signing the contract and Sheriff's Letter of Agency form, along with posting provided
  signage in the parking lot for No Trespassing, and signage on the business front
  window/entrance area for No Panhandling. Business shall obtain these forms from
   the City of Norwalk website and submit them via email to the Public Safety
  Department at shape@norwalkca.gov. All questions may be directed to Adriana
  Ortega via the same email or via phone at (562) 929-5730. The business is required
  to complete the forms and provided signage to be installed within 30 days of
  obtaining approvals.

11. Business owner/employees shall refrain from engaging in business transactions
  with individuals loitering and/or panhandling, so as to discourage them from
  frequenting the area.

12.Any graffiti painted or marked upon the premises shall be removed or painted within
  forty-eight (48) hours of the discovery thereof and or reported to the property
  manager for proper clean-up/removal.

13.Pre-recorded music at the outdoor patio, shall keep to the Norwalk Municipal Code
  requirements, Chapter 9.04, Article Ill. This item to be reviewed within 6 months to
  ensure compliance.

14.General noise complaints related to the operation of the business, will be addressed
  as needed, as per Norwalk Municipal Codes.
